outcome: Tunica media area of spiral artery
cohort: Thirty placentas (fifteen from mothers with preeclampsia and fifteen from healthy mothers) and their corresponding newborns were examined from a hospital in Babylon.
finding: The study found significant differences in the internal area and tunica media of the spiral artery in placentas from women with preeclampsia compared to healthy women, which was also associated with an impact on the baby's body weight (less than 2.5 kg).
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as the most common mode of childbirth for women with preeclampsia, and low birth weight was significantly associated with natural delivery in the control group.
cross-section timing: Placentas and birth weight data were collected at the time of birth.
birth_weight: Babies included in the study had birth weights, with low birth weight defined as fewer than 2.5 kg.
